column3: OWASP Artificial Intelligence Security Verification Standard (AISVS) 1.0
column8:
- AI systems introduce risks traditional appsec standards did not design for: prompt injection, poisoning, extraction, adversarial inputs, agentic action, RAG leakage, and model supply-chain integrity
- AISVS fills the gap between general ASVS/SCVS and AI-specific verification; it does not replace them
- Twelve control families with Level 1–3 verification depth aligned to matching ASVS levels
- Every requirement begins with "Verify that" and must be objectively testable through inspection, test, or audit
column9:
- General authentication, transport, logging, and SBOM controls stay in ASVS/SCVS; AISVS only restates them when AI-specific evidence differs
- Governance-only obligations (fairness docs, model cards without security tests) stay out of scope
- A requirement must address one concern implementable as one mechanism; no duplicate controls across chapters
- Prompt injection in agents combines C2, C7, C9, C10, C11, and C12 requirements together
column10:
- Assign each requirement to Level 1, 2, or 3 and verify AI apps at the same ASVS level in parallel
- Use Appendix B controls inventory to see which chapters jointly defend a given AI threat
- Mark out-of-scope requirements when a vendor model card is the only evidence available
- Integrate AISVS checks into CI/CD, code review, procurement questionnaires, and pen-test scopes

column3: SANS AI Security Maturity Model eBook
column8:
- Maturity spans three pillars: Protect AI, Utilize AI, and Govern AI, each with five stages from ad hoc to optimizing
- Governance acts as a ceiling: overall maturity cannot exceed the weakest pillar or Govern score
- Self-reported capabilities without documentary evidence are capped at Stage 2
- Model maps to NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, ISO 42001, OWASP AI Exchange, and CSA AI Controls Matrix
column9:
- A strong Protect or Utilize score cannot mask absent governance structure
- Stage claims require named prerequisites, metrics, and audit-defensible artifacts at every level
- Agentic AI guidance is embedded; agent deployments inherit the same pillar and cap rules
column10:
- Score each pillar separately with evidence before assigning a stage
- Apply cap rules so Protect and Govern imbalances surface in executive reporting
- Advance stage only when program indicators, people indicators, and metrics meet the workbook definition
- Use mapped external frameworks to produce regulator- and customer-ready maturity evidence
